changes.before: Give `.gallery` a grid display with three equal columns.

before: CSS Grid arranges content in rows and columns. The element with display: grid is the grid container; its direct children become grid items. A track is one row or column's space. grid-template-columns defines the columns. repeat(3, 1fr) means make three columns, each with one equal fraction of the remaining space. The browser places ordinary items across those columns in source order and starts new rows as needed. Grid is useful when both horizontal and vertical alignment matter, such as a photo gallery.

gap reserves space between tracks. Subtract the gaps before dividing the remaining width into equal fr shares. A 636px container with four columns and three 12px gaps leaves 600px for tracks, so each track gets 150px. If a question already gives 600px of track space and asks for three equal columns, divide 600 by three to get 200px. Track space and total container width are different when gaps exist. The fr unit is a share of available space, not a fixed number of pixels.

Grid lines mark track boundaries. For columns, lines are numbered starting at the first edge. grid-column: 2 places an item starting at column line 2, which begins the second column in this simple left-to-right grid. It does not mean row 2 or “two columns wide.” grid-column: 2 / 4 starts at line 2 and ends at line 4, spanning two tracks. grid-column: span 2 asks to span two columns without naming a starting line. A slash separates start and end in this property.

Put this fragment inside body and supply real image files. It works with the earlier gallery CSS. ```html
``` Each img is a direct grid item. class="gallery" selects the container. aria-label names the gallery region when applicable to its semantics, and each informative picture has its own alt description. Images need no closing img tag. Adding another image adds another item; the grid can create another row automatically.

A responsive layout changes when available space changes. The @media query here tests the viewport's width, not an individual image's width. Because it comes after the initial grid rule, its matching column declaration replaces the earlier one. Test just above, exactly at, and just below a threshold to understand max-width's inclusive limit. display: block avoids image baseline spacing, and height: auto avoids stretching the picture into a wrong shape. A narrow grid still needs sensible child content; long unbreakable content can require further sizing rules in other projects.

For the supplied gallery, use three equal columns and a gap above 480px, then two equal columns at 480px and below. Make every image width: 100% with height: auto. The checks count the final columns for the current viewport and compare the image width with its cell width after subtracting gaps. Resize across the threshold and inspect all rows for clipping. Explain why grid-column: 2 starts in the second column, then calculate an equal column width using track space before trying the project.
after: CSS Grid arranges items in rows and columns. Put `display: grid` on the element that holds the items. Its direct children become grid items.
`gap` leaves space between the columns and rows. The browser removes the gaps before sharing the space between columns. If 600 pixels remain for three equal columns, each gets 200 pixels.
Grid lines are the edges between columns. In a left-to-right grid, `grid-column: 3 / 5` starts at line 3 and ends at line 5. There are two columns between those lines.
The supplied gallery contains images. Give each image `width: 100%` to fill its column and `height: auto` to keep its shape. Each picture also needs a useful description in its HTML `alt` attribute.
A media query can change the number of columns. `max-width: 480px` applies at 480 pixels and below. The width belongs to the preview area, not to each photo.
Keep three columns above 480 pixels. Use two columns at 480 pixels and below. Check that the images fit and keep their shape.

before.question: In a simple left-to-right grid, an item has grid-column: 3 / 5. How many column tracks does it span?
before.explanation: It starts at line 3 and ends at line 5, spanning the two tracks between them. Line numbers are boundaries, not the number of tracks occupied.

after.question: An item starts at grid line 3 and ends at line 5. How many columns does it cover?
after.explanation: It covers the column from line 3 to 4 and the column from line 4 to 5: two columns.

project.title: A photo gallery
project.task: Arrange the photos in three columns, changing to two columns on a narrow screen.
project.done_when: The photos fit their columns, keep their shape, and pass the checks at both widths.
